data.title: Workspaces and Tenant Context
data.description: Use workspaces to keep businesses separated and avoid cross-tenant mistakes.
data.body:
Workspaces and Tenant Context

Use workspaces to keep businesses separated and avoid cross-tenant mistakes.

What this does

Explains how to confirm and switch workspace context safely.

Who can use it

Owner, Manager (based on access)

Before you start

• Ensure your account is mapped to the expected business workspaces.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Workspaces`.

2. Confirm current active workspace.

3. Switch workspace before editing inventory, sales, or settings.

4. Re-check page headers/context after switching.

What happens next

All data operations apply to the active workspace only.

Tips

• Make context checks routine before high-impact actions.

Common mistakes

• Updating settings in the wrong workspace during multi-business shifts.

Troubleshooting

• If data looks “missing,” verify you’re in the right workspace first.

Related articles

• `getting-started-first-week.md`

• `settings-and-aliases.md`

• `reports-and-insights.md`

data.title: Troubleshooting: Fast Fixes First
data.description: When something feels off, run this sequence before deep debugging.
data.body:
Troubleshooting: Fast Fixes First

When something feels off, run this sequence before deep debugging.

What this does

Gives a quick response path for the most common DRX issues.

Who can use it

All roles (within their access scope)

Before you start

• Capture what route failed and what action you took right before it.

Step-by-step

1. Confirm workspace and user role context.

2. Refresh the route and retry the action once.

3. Validate source data in supporting pages (sales, inventory, customer).

4. Check whether issue is permission, data, or flow-state related.

5. Escalate with exact route + timestamp + user role + action details.

What happens next

Most issues resolve quickly; escalations become cleaner when needed.

Tips

• Report with specifics, not “it broke.”

Common mistakes

• Jumping straight to manual data edits before confirming root cause.

Troubleshooting

• POS issue: confirm product visibility and session state.

• Inventory issue: compare intake/adjustments/sales.

• Access issue: verify role permission mapping.

Related articles

• `quick-pos-run-sale.md`

• `inventory-audit-fixes.md`

• `roles-permissions-staff-access.md`

data.title: Settings and Aliases: Keep Workflows Clean
data.description: Settings is where you lock in business config, team setup, and fast product lookup behavior.
data.body:
Settings and Aliases: Keep Workflows Clean

Settings is where you lock in business config, team setup, and fast product lookup behavior.

What this does

Covers key settings routes and alias management.

Who can use it

Owner, Manager

Before you start

• Confirm you’re in the correct workspace/business context.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Settings` for overview.

2. Update account/business details in `Settings > Profile`.

3. Manage team in `Settings > Team`.

4. Set item aliases in `Settings > Inventory > Aliases`.

5. Test alias behavior in `Quick Sale`.

What happens next

Cleaner aliases and settings reduce checkout friction and product confusion.

Tips

• Use alias patterns staff actually type.

• Keep one naming convention across top sellers.

Common mistakes

• Creating overlapping aliases for different products.

Troubleshooting

• If alias lookup is wrong, remove collisions and retest.

Related articles

• `quick-pos-run-sale.md`

• `inventory-manage-stock.md`

• `roles-permissions-staff-access.md`

data.title: Roles and Permissions: Keep Access Tight
data.description: Give people what they need to work, and nothing extra.
data.body:
Roles and Permissions: Keep Access Tight

Give people what they need to work, and nothing extra.

What this does

Explains how to manage staff access safely in DRX.

Who can use it

Owner, Manager (based on role control permissions)

Before you start

• Confirm who should be staff vs manager.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Settings > Team`.

2. Add or update staff profiles.

3. Assign the lowest role that still lets them do their job.

4. Review sensitive-action permissions regularly.

5. Remove access immediately on offboarding.

What happens next

Cleaner permissions reduce risk and prevent accidental high-impact actions.

Tips

• Review access during schedule changes and staffing updates.

Common mistakes

• Leaving manager access active after role changes.

Troubleshooting

• If a user can’t open expected pages, verify role mapping and permission checks.

• If access is too broad, drop role level first, then test.

Related articles

• `settings-and-aliases.md`

• `privacy-security-rtbf.md`

• `admin-tools-overview.md`

data.title: Sales History and Receipt Checks
data.description: This is where you confirm what sold, when it sold, and how the transaction landed.
data.body:
Sales History and Receipt Checks

This is where you confirm what sold, when it sold, and how the transaction landed.

What this does

Explains how to review completed sales and inspect transaction details.

Who can use it

Staff (own scope), Manager, Owner

Before you start

• At least one completed sale should exist.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Sales`.

2. Filter or search for the transaction.

3. Open a sale detail view from the list.

4. Verify line items, totals, and payment details.

5. Use this view to resolve customer disputes and shift reconciliation issues.

What happens next

Validated sale data supports reports, inventory movement, and audit checks.

Tips

• Check sale detail before editing inventory when counts look off.

Common mistakes

• Attempting to debug stock first without confirming the original sale record.

Troubleshooting

• If a sale is missing, verify date filters and role scope.

• If totals mismatch, re-check applied adjustments and payment state.

Related articles

• `quick-pos-run-sale.md`

• `reports-and-insights.md`

• `inventory-audit-fixes.md`

data.title: Inventory: Manage Stock Without Guessing
data.description: Track what came in, what went out, and what needs action now.
data.body:
Inventory: Manage Stock Without Guessing

Track what came in, what went out, and what needs action now.

What this does

Covers the main inventory workflow: overview, intake, and adjustment.

Who can use it

Manager, Owner (staff access depends on permissions)

Before you start

• Product records and units should be set.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Inventory` for current stock view.

2. Use `Inventory > Intake` to add incoming stock.

3. Use `Inventory > Adjust` for corrections (increase/decrease/set).

4. Add a clear reason on adjustments to keep traceability.

5. Re-check affected products in overview.

What happens next

Inventory updates feed sales availability and reporting accuracy.

Tips

• Write short but specific adjustment reasons.

• Intake in small, frequent batches instead of giant catch-up edits.

Common mistakes

• Using manual set-to adjustments when intake is the right move.

• Skipping reason fields.

Troubleshooting

• If counts drift, compare intake + adjustments + recent sales.

• If an item disappears in POS, verify product status and stock state.

Related articles

• `inventory-audit-fixes.md`

• `quick-pos-run-sale.md`

• `reports-and-insights.md`

data.title: Privacy and Security: Daily Controls + RTBF
data.description: Privacy in DRX is operational, not decorative. Use these controls to protect customer data and reduce risk.
data.body:
Privacy and Security: Daily Controls + RTBF

Privacy in DRX is operational, not decorative. Use these controls to protect customer data and reduce risk.

What this does

Covers privacy posture in normal usage plus user-deletion (RTBF) workflow.

Who can use it

Owner, approved admin roles

Before you start

• Confirm policy for data retention and deletion approvals.

Step-by-step

1. Review privacy-sensitive access in team/role settings.

2. Limit exposure of customer and financial data by role.

3. Use audit/trace surfaces for sensitive action review.

4. For deletion requests, run the RTBF path with tenant + user checks.

5. Confirm follow-up validation after deletion actions.

What happens next

You maintain compliance posture without breaking operator workflows.

Tips

• Handle deletion actions with a second-person review when possible.

Common mistakes

• Running deletions without validating tenant/user IDs.

Troubleshooting

• If deletion fails, verify route parameters and authorization context first.

Related articles

• `roles-permissions-staff-access.md`

• `admin-tools-overview.md`

• `troubleshooting-fast-fixes.md`

data.title: Quick POS: Run a Sale Fast
data.description: Quick POS is for getting in, making the sale, and keeping it moving.
data.body:
Quick POS: Run a Sale Fast

Quick POS is for getting in, making the sale, and keeping it moving.

What this does

Walks through the operator flow from `Quick Sale` to payment completion.

Who can use it

Staff, Manager, Owner (based on role permissions)

Before you start

• Product catalog should be active.

• User needs POS access permission.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Quick Sale`.

2. Add items by search or saved aliases.

3. Confirm quantities and remove mistakes before payment.

4. Continue to `Payment`.

5. Select payment method and confirm.

6. Finish on `Complete` and return for next sale.

What happens next

The sale posts to history and downstream reporting.

Tips

• Keep aliases clean for top items.

• Fix quantity before payment to avoid extra correction work.

Common mistakes

• Ringing with stale product info.

• Skipping final total check in rush periods.

Troubleshooting

• If item lookup is slow, simplify search terms or use aliases.

• If payment fails to post, confirm route state and session auth.

Related articles

• `sales-history-receipts.md`

• `settings-and-aliases.md`

• `troubleshooting-fast-fixes.md`

data.title: Inventory Audit: Fix Count Problems Fast
data.description: When the numbers feel off, this is the cleanup playbook.
data.body:
Inventory Audit: Fix Count Problems Fast

When the numbers feel off, this is the cleanup playbook.

What this does

Shows how to audit inventory movement and isolate bad counts.

Who can use it

Manager, Owner

Before you start

• Have access to inventory history and recent sales.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Inventory > Audit`.

2. Identify products with unexpected deltas.

3. Compare movement against `Sales` history.

4. Check recent `Intake` and `Adjust` actions.

5. Apply corrective adjustment with a clear reason.

What happens next

Corrected counts stabilize POS and restore trust in reports.

Tips

• Fix high-volume items first.

• Keep one person accountable for final correction approval per shift.

Common mistakes

• Editing values without documenting cause.

Troubleshooting

• If mismatch repeats, verify alias/sku collisions and duplicate product usage.

Related articles

• `inventory-manage-stock.md`

• `sales-history-receipts.md`

• `troubleshooting-fast-fixes.md`

data.title: Getting Started: Your First Week in DRX
data.description: DRX is built to help you sell fast, track inventory clean, and keep customer data under control without the noise.
data.body:
Getting Started: Your First Week in DRX

DRX is built to help you sell fast, track inventory clean, and keep customer data under control without the noise.

What this does

This guide gets your shop from fresh setup to daily use with the least friction.

Who can use it

Owner, Manager

Before you start

• Make sure your business workspace is created.

• Confirm owner account access works.

• Decide who needs manager vs staff access.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Dashboard` and confirm you can load business data.

2. Go to `Settings` and verify basic business details.

3. Open `Settings > Team` and invite staff accounts.

4. Add products from `Inventory`.

5. Set alias shortcuts in `Settings > Inventory > Aliases`.

6. Run a test checkout from `Quick Sale`.

7. Check `Sales` history to confirm the sale posted.

What happens next

You move into normal daily flow: Quick Sale, inventory updates, customer lookup, and end-of-day report checks.

Tips

• Start simple: add your most sold products first.

• Keep aliases short so staff can move fast on mobile.

Common mistakes

• Giving everyone manager-level access by default.

• Skipping test sales before going live.

Troubleshooting

• If `Quick Sale` won’t start, check auth/session and role access.

• If products don’t show in sale flow, check product status in `Inventory`.

Related articles

• `quick-pos-run-sale.md`

• `inventory-manage-stock.md`

• `roles-permissions-staff-access.md`

data.title: Dashboard: Daily Check in 2 Minutes
data.description: Use the dashboard to see what moved today, what needs attention, and what might break your shift later.
data.body:
Dashboard: Daily Check in 2 Minutes

Use the dashboard to see what moved today, what needs attention, and what might break your shift later.

What this does

Gives a fast read on sales flow, inventory pressure, and operation health.

Who can use it

Owner, Manager

Before you start

• You need access to the main app dashboard route.

• Make sure data is syncing from sales and inventory flows.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Dashboard`.

2. Check high-level sales activity first.

3. Review low-stock or risk signals tied to inventory.

4. Spot-check credit or balance exposure if you run front/balance flows.

5. Use dashboard findings to decide what to fix next in `Inventory`, `Sales`, or `Reports`.

What happens next

You jump directly into the right queue instead of chasing problems blind.

Tips

• Start every shift with dashboard first, reports second.

• Use dashboard for triage, then verify details in route-specific pages.

Common mistakes

• Treating dashboard numbers as final audit numbers without checking source pages.

Troubleshooting

• If numbers look off, compare `Sales` records and inventory change history.

• If cards are empty, verify role permissions and data ingestion.

Related articles

• `reports-and-insights.md`

• `inventory-audit-fixes.md`

• `sales-history-receipts.md`

• You need access to the main app dashboard route.

• Make sure data is syncing from sales and inventory flows.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Dashboard`.

2. Check high-level sales activity first.

3. Review low-stock or risk signals tied to inventory.

4. Spot-check credit or balance exposure if you run front/balance flows.

5. Use dashboard findings to decide what to fix next in `Inventory`, `Sales`, or `Reports`.

What happens next

You jump directly into the right queue instead of chasing problems blind.

Tips

• Start every shift with dashboard first, reports second.

• Use dashboard for triage, then verify details in route-specific pages.

Common mistakes

• Treating dashboard numbers as final audit numbers without checking source pages.

Troubleshooting

• If numbers look off, compare `Sales` records and inventory change history.

• If cards are empty, verify role permissions and data ingestion.

data.title: Front / Balances: Credit and Payment Workflow
data.description: This is where you track who owes, who paid, and what still needs follow-up.
data.body:
Front / Balances: Credit and Payment Workflow

This is where you track who owes, who paid, and what still needs follow-up.

What this does

Covers credit sale handling, balance tracking, and payment logging.

Who can use it

Manager, Owner (and staff if explicitly permitted)

Before you start

• Credit flow must be enabled for your business policy.

• Customer record should exist for balance tracking.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Credit`.

2. Review open balances and overdue accounts.

3. Record new credit-linked transactions using approved flow.

4. Record incoming payments against the right customer balance.

5. Re-check totals after each payment post.

What happens next

Balances update and become visible for follow-up and reporting.

Tips

• Verify customer identity before applying payment.

• Keep payment notes clean for audit trails.

Common mistakes

• Posting a payment to the wrong customer record.

Troubleshooting

• If balance doesn’t update, refresh and verify payment route response.

• If overdue logic looks wrong, validate transaction dates and role visibility scope.

Related articles

• `customers-profiles-history.md`

• `reports-and-insights.md`

• `roles-permissions-staff-access.md`

data.body:
Admin Tools Overview

Admin routes are for high-impact controls: feature gating, approvals, and system-level visibility.

What this does

Summarizes the admin area and when to use each section.

Who can use it

Admin-authorized users only

Before you start

• Confirm you have explicit admin route access.

Step-by-step

1. Open `Admin` dashboard.

2. Use `Admin > Users` for access-level interventions.

3. Use `Admin > Features` for feature gate review.

4. Use `Admin > Approvals` for controlled actions.

5. Use audit/admin analytics surfaces to trace sensitive changes.

What happens next

Admin actions affect broad user behavior. Keep logs and change rationale tight.

Tips

• Treat admin changes like production changes: small, traceable, reversible where possible.

Common mistakes

• Rolling out feature toggles without a validation pass on target roles.

Troubleshooting

• If a feature appears missing for users, inspect feature gate + role + tenant context.

Related articles

• `roles-permissions-staff-access.md`

• `privacy-security-rtbf.md`

• `drx-intelligence.md`
